clue.text: Pilot must visit planet and snare dangerous organism

indicators.note: the pilot calls on the planet, so it comes after it

parts.note: Venus, the second planet from the sun
to fly is to pilot an aircraft
a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: An astronaut must land on Venus and capture some deadly alien life form.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilot is a verb here, giving FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnivorous plant traps and digests insects, so it is deadly to its prey.

clue.text: We see love endlessly arising — can love erupt like this?

definitions.text: We see love endlessly arising — can love erupt like this?

indicators.note: in a down answer, arising means reading upwards, so backwards
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, giving the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic wonders whether passion can explode like a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a mountain whose fire might be what erupting love looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano is the mountain that erupts, the picture the clue paints of passion boiling over.

clue.text: Redundant, finally free of small torments

indicators.note: the word drops the small at its very end

parts.note: needless means unnecessary or redundant

explanation.surface: Someone made redundant is at last free of petty worries.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or provoke them, so needles is a verb meaning torments.

clue.text: Times of innocence and fantasy — add a lass to cuddle up!

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
words that cuddle the answer hold it inside them, so it is hidden in the run of letters

parts.note: the answer hides backwards across the end of fantasy and most of add a lass

explanation.surface: A dreamy invitation to add a girlfriend and snuggle up.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads like an anagram invitation, but the answer is hidden backwards in the words just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days is Shakespeare's phrase for youthful inexperience, the green and naive time of life.

clue.text: In the middle of July, craft something to wear

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the words July and craft

parts.note: the answer spans the end of July and the start of craft

explanation.surface: In midsummer, making an item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the stretchy fabric used for sportswear, so a garment made of it is clothing.

clue.text: Paper boat travelling around lake — passport needed?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the lake
a boat travelling has its letters moving about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a passport is a form of identification, ID

explanation.surface: A paper boat sailing round a lake — would it need a passport?
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper in small format, often called a paper.

clue.text: Prince of Wales maybe discussed high post? …

indicators.note: when discussed, the phrase is spoken out loud and sounds like the answer

parts.note: the Prince of Wales is a male heir to the throne

explanation.surface: The Prince of Wales perhaps talked about a lofty position.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, heir male runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is letters carried by aircraft, post that travels high up.

clue.text: .. One takes turns traditionally, could be Harry's spin

parts.note: Harry Potter, the boy wizard, so Harry's is Potter's
to wheel is to spin or turn round

explanation.surface: Something that rotates in the old way could be the boy wizard's twirl.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link this clue to 6 down, but the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A potter's wheel is the revolving disc on which clay is thrown, the craft's traditional turning device.

clue.text: Energy provider's message for sunbathers?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: advice to sunbathers to apply oil thoroughly

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into an instruction: oil (yourself) well.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled well producing petroleum is a source of fuel; read as a command it tells sunbathers to cover themselves in lotion.

clue.text: Clubs with a bar and French entertainment

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
et is French for and

explanation.surface: Nightclubs with a bar and French-style shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a show of songs and comedy staged in a club, a kind of live amusement.

clue.text: Access by retaining old ticket payment

indicators.note: the first word keeps the old inside it

parts.note: by means of, as in through
a fare is what is paid for a travel ticket

explanation.surface: Getting in by holding onto an outdated ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a road or route that gives passage through a place.

clue.text: Food shop design about to be drawn

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen
design as in art

explanation.surface: A delicatessen's design is about to be sketched.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawn here means pulled along behind, not sketched.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail something is to drag or pull it behind you, so trailed means hauled along.

clue.text: Carve once and you will regularly go for this food

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words

parts.note: the second, fourth and every alternate letter spell the answer

explanation.surface: Slice it once and you'll keep coming back for this dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a fruit eaten as a savoury dish, in salads or on toast.

clue.text: Heard satnav directions perhaps in background

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a satnav gives routes to follow

explanation.surface: Voice instructions from a satnav playing in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: In many British accents route rhymes with boot.
explanation.definitionFit: One's roots are one's origins and family heritage, one's background.

clue.text: Hiding in cellar, mad illogical creature

indicators.note: the answer lurks inside the run of the words that follow

parts.note: the answer spans the end of cellar, all of mad and the start of illogical

explanation.surface: A crazed, irrational beast lurking in a basement.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Alternative Of Mice and Men — half of that is filling

indicators.note: an alternative version of the title means its letters are rearranged
half of that takes its second two letters

explanation.surface: A spoof retitling of Steinbeck's Of Mice and Men, with talk of filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative' rearranges MICE and MEN into MINCEME, and 'half of' takes AT from 'that'. 'Of' and 'and' are just the title's words, used as links.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the mix of dried fruit and spices that goes inside mince pies, a sweet stuffing.

clue.text: Was sock, back to front, in sink?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter is moved from the back to the front

parts.note: to sock is to hit, to bash
taken as written

explanation.surface: Was the sock put in the sink back to front?
explanation.walkthrough: Sock looks like a garment but is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is a bowl with taps for washing the hands and face, a bathroom sink.

clue.text: Jogs in street, one's hill run oddly being over

parts.note: one's, read as one is, is I'm

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means turned over, so read backwards
oddly takes alternate letters of the words, here the ones in even places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jogger runs uphill in the street, one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: Jogs is a noun here: prompts or nudges, not runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that prompt a response, as a jog to the memory does.

clue.text: Boost body with soup? Not so

parts.note: a person's build is their body shape

indicators.note: not so means the word soup without the letters of so

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of so are taken out of soup

explanation.surface: Improving your physique with soup? Not really.
explanation.definitionFit: A build-up is an increase or strengthening, a boost.

clue.text: Bound to neglect new branch

indicators.note: neglecting new means leaving out that letter

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.surface: A leap that ignores fresh growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small twig or shoot, a little branch of a plant.

clue.text: Satire showing elite troops holding a Catholic mass

indicators.note: the troops hold the pieces inside them

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
RC, Roman Catholic
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mockery from special forces who take a Catholic service hostage.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like the Catholic service but is just M.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is biting, mocking irony, the tone of satire.

clue.text: University's welcomed in Caruso — unexpectedly rough

indicators.note: the university is taken inside the jumbled name
unexpectedly suggests the letters land in a surprising order

parts.note: Enrico Caruso, the famous tenor
U for university; the 's is is, joining it to the verb

explanation.surface: A university hosts the great tenor, who turns out to sound hoarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous means harsh and loud, a rough-sounding noise.

clue.text: Evokes breakdown of cities when Left gets in

indicators.note: the left gets inside the rearranged letters
breaking the word down scatters its letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political left gaining power stirs up urban collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response, which is to evoke it.

clue.text: Band of constituents heading north

indicators.note: in a down answer, heading north means the word is read upwards

parts.note: constituents are component parts

explanation.surface: A musical group of voters travelling north.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip of leather or fabric, a band used to fasten things.

clue.text: Cockney judge married upper-class females, finding one warmer

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it; a Cockney drops the H
U means upper-class in British usage
F for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: An East End magistrate who wed posh women discovers a heater.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is London working-class speech, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: An earmuff is a padded cover that keeps the ear warm in cold weather.

clue.text: Clean three articles from France and Germany

parts.note: the French articles la and un
der, the German definite article, completes the three

explanation.surface: Tidy up three items of goods from France and Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles means grammatical articles, the words for the and a, not items.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash them, making them clean.

clue.text: Delight of Caesar, say, holding united Spain back

indicators.note: the whole is read backwards
the Roman holds united inside

parts.note: Julius Caesar is an example of a Roman

explanation.surface: Caesar's joy at gripping a united Spain once more.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the international vehicle code for Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to charm or captivate someone, to delight them.

clue.text: Deploying map, I pop south to find famous character in Africa

indicators.note: deploying sets out the letters in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller unfolds a map and heads south to meet a celebrity in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippo is one of Africa's best-known big animals, a celebrated wildlife figure.
